Synopsis:
    U.S. Energy Secretary Wright and GE Vernova signed an energy rehabilitation deal with Venezuela, targeting stabilisation of the Venezuelan power grid within 6–12 months, with 1 GW of new capacity online within 24 months and an additional 5 GW over the following four years. Key focus is restoring degraded infrastructure including the Guri Dam (currently at ~50% design capacity). Grid stress is compounded by drought (El Niño), aging assets, and post-earthquake disruption. Political risk remains, with opposition leader Machado questioning investor credibility under the current government.
